newsitem.title: YEMEN: At least five European tourists abducted in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: At least five European tourists abducted in Yemen.

text.p: At least five European tourists have been kidnapped by tribesmen in southern Yemen, security and diplomatic sources said on Thursday.
"There has certainly been a kidnapping, and it seems to involve six people," a European diplomat told Reuters. "They were initially thought to be German, but are most probably Italian."
A Yemeni security official said earlier the incident involved at least five German tourists.
"They were on a tour in the Abyan governorate when they were kidnapped and taken to Shabwa (in central Yemen)," he said.
The official gave no further details on the second abduction of European tourists this month.
An Italian kidnapped by tribesmen earlier this month was released on Sunday after being held for several days. Two other Italian tourists were abducted in late July but were let go after one day.
In March, four German holidaymakers were kidnapped. Earlier that month a group of seven German motorcycle tourists were also abducted.
Kidnapping is a common tactic by Yemeni tribes holding grievances against the government or foreign oil firms operating in Yemen, one of the Arab world's poorest countries.

Tribesmen have tried to use hostages -- who have included French and U.S. diplomats and a Saudi ambassador -- as bargaining chips in mostly land and water disputes. All hostages have been released unharmed so far.
